questions.question: What does the trailer air supply control look like?

options.text: It is a square blue knob.
It is a triangular yellow knob.
It is an eight-sided red knob.
It is a circular orange knob.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is an eight-sided red knob.
questions.explanation: The trailer air supply control on newer vehicles is an eight-sided red knob. It controls the tractor protection valve.

questions.question: In a vehicle with an automatic tractor protection valve, when does the valve pop out?

options.text: When air pressure drops to between 20 and 45 psi.
When wheels regain traction after a skid.
When air pressure is above 45 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: When air pressure drops to between 20 and 45 psi.
questions.explanation: The automatic tractor protection valve pops out when air pressure drops to between 20 and 45 psi. When this happens, the protection valve closes and stops the flow of air.

questions.question: When coupling a trailer, what should you do?

options.text: Any glad hand can connect to any other glad hand.
Only connect one set of glad hands.

questions.explanation: Always connect matching glad hands. They are usually color-coded to prevent mistakes. Blue is typically used for service lines and red is used for emergency lines.

questions.question: When driving a bobtail tractor, what should you know?

options.text: Bobtails cannot drive as fast as tractors with semitrailers.
Bobtails take longer to stop than tractors with semitrailers.
Bobtails are illegal in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bobtails take longer to stop than tractors with semitrailers.
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor without a semitrailer attached. Bobtails are harder to stop and need a longer distance to come to a complete stop than tractors with loaded semitrailers.

questions.question: When a combination vehicle goes around a corner, what happens?

options.text: The turn should be as tight as possible.
The front and rear wheels follow different paths.
The rear wheels should run over the curb.
It is acceptable to knock over street signs if they are too close to the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear wheels follow different paths.
questions.explanation: When turning, the rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels. This is called off-tracking. This effect is more noticeable on vehicles with trailers.

questions.question: When connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer, what should the trailer height be?

options.text: Slightly higher than the center of the fifth wheel.
Level with the center of the fifth wheel.
Slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.
Next to the center of the fifth wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: The trailer should be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel when connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer.

questions.question: If a trailer is too high, what happens?

options.text: It will not make a difference when coupling.
The coupling will be more secure.

questions.explanation: Before coupling a tractor and trailer, check that the trailer height is correct. A trailer that is too low can damage the trailer nose. A trailer that is too high may not couple correctly.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?

options.text: When a truck driver is driving too fast.
When the vehicle in front of a truck is moving too slowly.
When a truck driver is driving too slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: When a truck driver is driving too fast.
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when a vehicle is driven too fast. To reduce rollover risk, load cargo low to the ground and drive slowly around turns and curves.

questions.question: Compared to empty rigs, fully-loaded rigs are:

options.text: Just as likely to roll over.

questions.explanation: Fully-loaded rigs have a higher center of gravity from the cargo weight. They are 10 times more likely to roll over in a crash than empty rigs.

questions.question: Air pressure in the ____ air line is controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake.
questions.explanation: The service air line is controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake. It is also called the control line or signal line. This line connects to relay valves, which make trailer brakes apply faster.

questions.question: Why does a lightly-loaded combination vehicle stop more slowly than a fully-loaded vehicle?

options.text: Stiff suspension springs and strong brakes give high traction.
Stiff suspension springs and strong brakes give low traction.
Brakes only work when a trailer reaches a minimum weight.
Suspension springs only work when a trailer reaches a minimum weight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stiff suspension springs and strong brakes give low traction.
questions.explanation: An empty combination vehicle stops more slowly than a fully-loaded vehicle. With less weight, the suspension springs and brakes have less traction than they would with a heavier load.

questions.question: Trailers with low underneath clearance are difficult to drive:
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are difficult to cross with a low-clearance trailer. Low-slung units and single-axle tractors pulling long trailers are especially challenging to drive over raised crossings.

questions.question: A shut-off valve:

options.text: Is on the front of a trailer.
Stops air from leaving the air brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops air from leaving the air brake system.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow between trailers. The rear shut-off valve should always be closed to prevent air from leaving the braking system.

questions.question: A combination vehicle has:
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles have two air lines: a service line and an emergency line.

questions.question: Driving a combination vehicle ____ than driving a single vehicle.
questions.explanation: Driving a combination vehicle requires more skill than driving a single vehicle. Combination vehicles are longer and heavier than single commercial vehicles.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: Makes it easier to turn a large vehicle.

questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops your wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: A trailer is most likely to swing around when:
questions.explanation: An empty trailer takes longer to stop than a loaded trailer. An empty or lightly-loaded trailer is most likely to swing out and hit other vehicles.

questions.question: Push in the trailer air supply control to:
questions.explanation: Push in the trailer air supply control to send air to the trailer. Pull out the trailer air supply control to turn off the air supply and activate the emergency brakes.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve:

options.text: Should always be used for parking.
Should only be used for parking on a downhill.
Should never be used for parking.
Should only be used when transporting cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should never be used for parking.
questions.explanation: Do not use the trailer hand valve for parking. It can cause all air to leak out of the braking system, making the brakes release. Use the parking brake instead.

questions.question: After finishing a pre-trip inspection, you should:

options.text: Leave the rear shut-off valves open.
Leave the emergency line valve open.

questions.explanation: Before driving, open the rear emergency line and service line shut-off valves to check for air leaks. Close both shut-off valves before you start driving.
